Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing the * followed by 1 on your telephone keypad. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Dynamics' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Sarah Kline, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act. Actual results could differ materially due to various risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of these factors.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Global Aerospace Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense, space, and commercial aviation. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering sustained value to our shareholders. Today, I'll highlight our overall company performance and key takeaways, analyze revenue drivers and headwinds, review book-to-bill ratios, discuss program margins and cost performance, outline strategic priorities and outlook, and touch on key guidance assumptions before handing over to John for deeper financial details.

Starting with overall performance highlights, Q3 capped off a banner nine months where we achieved industry-leading growth amid resilient defense spending and accelerating commercial recovery. We reported record quarterly revenue of $22.1 billion, up 12% year-over-year, driven by strong execution across our portfolio with sustained defense budget tailwinds and commercial aviation rebound. Adjusted diluted EPS hit $6.80, a 25% increase from last year, while free cash flow reached $2.8 billion, up 35% year-over-year, underscoring our operational discipline. Our remaining performance obligations stood at a historic $168 billion at quarter-end, up significantly year-over-year, complemented by robust book-to-bill visibility reflecting strong demand across Defense Systems, Commercial Aviation, and Space & Advanced Technologies segments. Margins expanded to segment-adjusted operating averages of 14.2%, up 180 basis points, thanks to favorable mix, supply chain efficiencies, and higher-volume production on programs like F-35 sustainment and NGAD enablers.

Defense Systems, comprising 55% of revenue, delivered standout results with elevated global tensions from Russia-Ukraine to Indo-Pacific dynamics around Taiwan fueling growth. U.S. DoD funding provided bedrock support, including a $1.2 billion IDIQ for hypersonic boost-glide components positioning us as a Tier 1 alongside primes. International sales surged 28%, driven by NATO's 2% GDP pledges—Poland and Finland contributed $250 million in integrated air defense akin to Patriot PAC-3 MSE upgrades—with margins expanding to 15.8% via digital thread productivity gains cutting manufacturing cycles 22% on missiles. Commercial Aviation, at 30% of the mix, posted surging revenue as air traffic rebounded to 95% of pre-pandemic levels per IATA, with aerostructures and avionics for Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo ramping deliveries 30% to 450 shipsets; supply chain on-time rates hit 90% for titanium and PCBs, boosting aftermarket MRO 40%, and our Gen 3 composite wing spar for 777X offers 15% weight savings now in low-rate production. Space & Advanced Technologies grew robustly despite peer launch delays, with $600 million NASA Orion propulsion modules, Blue Origin New Glenn upper stages, and $180 million DoD Phase 2 for 300kW solid-state lasers aligning with Army indirect fires protection; margins at 12.5% reflect dual-use tech like SDA Tranche 2 satellites.

Balance sheet strength persists with $12 billion in cash equivalents and net debt to EBITDA at 1.2x; we returned $1.2 billion to shareholders via buybacks and our 12th consecutive dividend increase to $1.20 per share. CapEx focused on Huntsville hypersonics and Fort Worth composites expansions. Regionally, North America drove 72%, Europe rose to 18% on F-35 for UK/Italy, Asia-Pacific to 7% via Japan GCAP, and emerging markets 3% with UAE THAAD. Key takeaways: structural demand tailwinds with global defense at $2.4 trillion per SIPRI and Boeing/Airbus forecasting 42,000 jets; technical leadership via additive manufacturing producing 15,000 parts and eVTOL hybrid propulsion passing FAA gates; disciplined allocation fueling ROIC to 18.5%, with opportunistic M&A in C4ISR.

Transitioning to revenue drivers and headwinds, Q3 revenue of $22.1 billion rose 12% year-over-year and exceeded guidance, marking six straight double-digit quarters with book-to-bill at 1.2x and backlog at $168 billion. Defense Systems at 62% or $13.7 billion grew 18%, led by F-35 Lot 15 ramps recognizing $1.2 billion plus $4.5 billion Lot 16-18 awards; international F-35 to Israel/Japan added $450 million amid Indo-Pacific tensions. Hypersonics like AGM-183A ARRW unlocked $800 million post-testing, JASSM-ER $650 million from $60 billion Ukraine aid, bookings over $2 billion pushing backlog to $85 billion. Commercial Aerospace at 28% or $6.2 billion surged 22%, engine shipments for 737 MAX/A320neo up 15% to 320 units capturing 45% share, aftermarket MRO/digital twins $900 million as traffic hits 98% of 2019. Space grew 9% on GPS IIIF and $1.2 billion Vulcan Centaur. U.S. 68%, Europe 18% on FCAS, Asia-Pacific 12% via AUKUS.

Headwinds included supply chain disruptions trimming 200 bps—titanium 20% short from Russia-Ukraine, mitigated by dual-sourcing 150 tons from Japan/India and 18-month inventory; labor shortages deferred $150 million F-35 via 1,200 new hires targeting 95% fill; ITAR delays $200 million Saudi hypersonics; Boeing 737 caps pressuring 5-7% volumes offset by Airbus; inflation adding 150 bps COGS shielded by 75% fixed-price backlog yielding 12.4% operating profit up 80 bps. Forward, $500 million additive for hypersonics cuts leads 40%, AI supply platform at 92% accuracy.

On book-to-bill, overall 1.18x quarterly and 1.22x year-to-date—strongest since Q1 2022—with $28.7 billion bookings vs. $23.5 billion sales adding $5 billion net backlog to $162 billion, 85% visibility to 2028. Geopolitics drives: $850 billion DoD FY25, Ukraine/Israel aid, NATO 2%, Taiwan tensions capturing share from Rafael/MBDA. $2.5 billion R&D wins premium on CCA/NGAD hypersonics; dual-sourced titanium de-risks vs. peers.

By segment, adapting to our core: Aeronautics/DMS at 1.32x quarterly/1.35x YTD on $4.8 billion bookings vs. $3.6 billion sales—$2.2 billion F-35 Block 4 IDIQ (1,200+ LRIP tooled), $1.1 billion PAC-3 MSE for Houthi threats; YTD backlog $68 billion up 12%, international 22% via Poland HIMARS/Australia AUKUS, margins 14.2% up 120 bps on MBSE cutting labor 18%, FY26 $145 billion missile line >70% share. Missiles/SAI 1.15x/1.20x, $2.9 billion booked vs. $2.5 billion, backlog $42 billion up 10%—$900 million GPS IIIF PNT, $650 million GEO from Intelsat/SES; U.S. 65%, APAC Japan QZSS, photonics 10x RF throughput NASA Artemis win, 95% launch assurance vs. Starship delays, 2025 EPS accretion. Commercial/Rotary/CAM 0.98x quarterly/1.05x YTD, backlog $32 billion—$1.4 billion 777X wings/composites from 787, $450 million eVTOL Joby/Archer, MRO 35% up, China C919 $300 million; sustainability hybrid/SAF targeting 20% green by 2027, 12-14% margins best-in-class as deliveries rebound to 1,400/year. Raised FY24 to 1.20x overall. 

Program margins hit 11.8% overall, up 130 bps YoY/40 bps sequentially—strongest since Q4 2021—via cost discipline, mix, learning curves. Aeronautics 12.4% up 160 bps: F-35 Lots 15/16 13.2% CPI 1.08 $285 million variance, wing automation 18% improvement absorbing 12% titanium inflation via Spirit/Triumph deals; KC-46 10.9% SPI 0.97 $150 million EAC cuts Teamcenter ECOs down 35%; F-35 FMS Israel/Poland high teens offsetting Boeing ripples; NGAD FPD 8.5% recovering $420 million FAR changes. Missiles/Fire Control 14.6% up 220 bps: LRASM Block 2 16.8% CPI 1.12 GE Additive 22% cost-out; JASSM/ARRW $1.8 billion UARCs 15%+; PrSM 15.2% Raytheon seekers; Middle East FMS Patriot GEM-T 17%; $510 million underruns, 'Skills Forward' 2,400 machinists vs. 6.5% inflation. Space 9.2% improving: Orion 10.1% SPI 0.95 $340 million Merlin reusability MBSE BOEs down 28%; GPS IIIF 11.5% GaN 92% yields; Artemis $4.7 billion floor, AUKUS BAE 12%; rare earths mitigated DLA 1,200 suppliers 85% dual. Trends: 7% volume, fixed leverage R&D 4.1%, 15% sustainment shift 42% backlog; 450 bps productivity Lean/AI Palantir 95% accuracy vs. 5.8% labor/7.2% materials inflation. FY24 11.0-11.5%.

Strategically, priorities center on defense acceleration amid $923 billion FY25 NDAA 4.1% up—F-35 Lot 17 ahead, NGAD 1.3x FFP; Europe NATO €2 trillion 25% backlog Eastern PAC-3 Poland/Romania €1.2 billion, Indo-Pacific ARRW-like hypersonics Japan/Australia $800 million, Middle East IAMD UAE/Israel 18% Iron Dome. Supply resilience: titanium/rare earths down 35% dual-sourcing Red Sea mitigations; commercial 737/A320neo 45/month from 32, GTF 95% adherence, MRO APAC 7% CAGR. Next-gen IR&D 4.2%: DEWs/CCA/pLEO HACM Mach 8 $5 billion IDIQ, Golden Dome AI NSSL $2.3 billion, hybrid eVTOL SAF 25% emissions cut. Q4 revenues $18.1 billion +7% QoQ/9% YoY, EPS $2.65-$2.75 +5%, FCF $1.4 billion; FY25 $74-76 billion +8-10%, margins 11.5-12.0% +150 bps, EPS $11.50-12.00, book-to-bill 1.15-1.20x. $8 billion cash, 75% FCF returns $4 billion buybacks.

Guidance assumptions: FY24 revenue $88-92 billion +8-12%, EPS $28.50-30.00 +10-15%, margins 12.5-13.5% +50-100 bps, FCF $9-11 billion on $145 billion backlog +5% seq. Defense 55% $48-51 billion: $850 billion DoD no sequestration, F-35 Lot 16 $12 billion DOT&E slips 3-6 months, Ukraine $60 billion Javelin 4,000/month, Middle East $15 billion Iron Dome/Patriot 25% share, NATO 15%, AUKUS $2 billion; titanium $25-30/kg labor 4% offset 10% digital NGAD. Commercial 30% $26-29 billion: RPKs 7-9% narrowbody 85% on-time, 737 38/month 787 5/month A320neo 50/month no LEAP slips, aftermarket 12% 60 million hours MRO +5%, China 20% APAC vs. Europe fuel $2.80; GTF risk $500 million hedged $4 billion backlog. Space 15% $14-16 billion: Artemis 2026 Orion $1.2 billion, Starlink $800 million SRM, NSSP $28 billion PWSA TR-1A vs. Northrop; hypersonic 150 bps AI C4ISR 8% costs. Cross: 2-3% pricing sustainment 70% F-35, SG&A 8.5% R&D $2.8 billion DEW/CCA, FX 1% hedge 70% VSMPO, $4-5 billion repurchases 40% dividend. Fortress $8 billion cash vs. CRs DPA grants; risks shutdowns/CASB/China rare earths 20%, Ukraine >$100 billion +$1-2 EPS.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to establish next-generation air dominance, driving our future growth. Strong demand persists for defense systems, and commercial aerospace is recovering steadily.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Sarah. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $22.1 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted earnings per share were $6.80. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $12 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains raised at $88-92 billion revenue, adjusted EBITDA margins 13.5-14.0% implying EPS $28.50-$30.00, incorporating $1.2 billion favorable performance offset by titanium/labor. FY25 outlook $74-76 billion. We're actively managing costs, investing in growth, returning capital via $4 billion repurchases and dividends.

Specific highlights include gross margin of 22.5%, up 130 bps; operating income $4.9 billion, up 15%; free cash flow $2.8 billion.

To elaborate by segment for FY24 guidance: Aeronautics $32-34 billion +10-12% YoY, EBITDA 11-12%—F-35/NGAD engine supply up to 156 deliveries, U.S. DoD 65% $12 billion NGAD R&D, international 25% backlog UK/Israel $4.2 billion, Indo-Pacific AUKUS CCA $2 billion FY25, $1.5 billion digital twins -30% LRIP risks, margins +150 bps fixed-price, U.S. shutdown watch. Missiles/Fire Control $18-20 billion +15-18%, 14-15%—hypersonics $3.5 billion double prior, JASSM/ARRW FRP Q4, U.S. 70% Ukraine $10 billion PAC-3/SM-6, exports Saudi/Poland $1.8 billion Asia $5 billion PAC-3, GPI MDA BlackSky SRM, 20% volume Raytheon infra $200 million inflation clauses. Rotary/Mission $14-15 billion flat-+3%, 10-11%—CH-47/MH-60R $2.1 billion Block II, U.S. Army 55% Australia LAND 4503/India Apache, Europe Germany $800 million Chinooks, Matrix autonomy V-280 25% labor FY26, titanium delays $300 million FY25 recovery. Space $14-15 billion +5-8%, 12-13%—GPS IIIF/Vulcan 12 milestones $1.2 billion pLEO DoD, U.S. Space Force/NRO 80% $4 billion warning sats, UK Skynet/France $900 million AUKUS pillar 2, Tranche 3 PWSA 100 Gbps optical, ULA synergies launch risks. Commercial $10-12 billion +25-30%, 8-9%—737 MAX/787 45 fuselages 380 narrow/75 widebody, North America/China 60% Airbus ramp, Middle East MRO +40%, CFM LEAP/777X $500 million, bottlenecks ease 38/month cap.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, John. Operationally, we've seen significant supply chain improvements, stabilizing titanium forgings and rare earths via dual-sourcing from U.S./allied vendors reducing exposure 35%, enabling production ramps on F-35 Lots 17, hypersonics to full-rate, and 737/A320neo to 45 ships monthly. Investments in automation, digital thread, and AI predictive analytics have boosted forecast accuracy to 92-95%, cutting cycle times 22-35% and labor 18-25%, with Lean Six Sigma yielding 450 bps productivity. Huntsville and Fort Worth expansions support hypersonics and composites, targeting 95% fill rates via 1,200+ apprenticeships despite 6-8% wage inflation.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Maria. On technology, we're advancing next-gen propulsion with F135 improvements for 156 F-35s, Merlin reusability analogs, and GE Additive for hypersonic nozzles reducing leads 40%; photonics optical comms 10x RF for Artemis/GPS IIIF GaN 92% yields; Matrix autonomy for V-280/CCA; HACM Mach 8 wind tunnels; AI/ML C4ISR predictive maintenance 8% costs; directed energy 300kW lasers; Golden Dome pLEO mesh NSSL; hybrid-electric eVTOL/SAF emissions 25% down; digital twins/Model-Based Systems Engineering slashing BOEs/ECOs 28-35%. These provide competitive edges for NGAD, PWSA, AAM $1T TAM.

Robert Chen:
Thank you, Elena. Strategically, we're evaluating acquisitions in C4ISR, European missiles post-Rheinmetall, bolt-ons <$1 billion to complement portfolio and expand reach. Developing models for sustainment/services now 42% backlog, dual-use space commercialization, sustainability 20% green by 2027, AUKUS pillar 2/Quad pacts. Positioning for FY26 $145 billion missile modernization >70% share, NSSL Phase 3, HACM $5 billion IDIQ via IP moats in AESA radars/AI mission/orbital tech.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Instructions for queuing: press * then 1. Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the revenue and earnings guidance by segment, especially Aeronautics and hypersonics ramps?

Sarah Kline:
Certainly, Mike. As John detailed, Aeronautics guides $32-34 billion with 11-12% margins on 156 F-35 deliveries amid Pratt & Whitney supply fixes, $12 billion NGAD R&D, international NATO 25% backlog up from 20% with UK/Israel $4.2 billion and AUKUS CCA $2 billion FY25; digital engineering $1.5 billion cuts LRIP risks 30%, margins +150 bps despite shutdown risks. Missiles $18-20 billion 14-15% on hypersonics doubling to $3.5 billion JASSM/ARRW FRP Q4, Ukraine $10 billion PAC-3/SM-6, exports $1.8 billion Saudi/Poland Asia $5 billion, GPI demos leveraging BlackSky SRM with $200 million inflation protections. These reflect better ramps, wins, supply stabilization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about book-to-bill trends by segment and any supply chain updates?

John Harlan:
Laura, overall 1.18x Q3/1.22x YTD adds $5 billion backlog to $162-168 billion. Defense/DMS/Aeronautics/Missiles stellar 1.32x/1.35x on F-35 Block 4 $2.2 billion, PAC-3 $1.1 billion, Poland HIMARS/AUKUS international 22%, backlog $68 billion. Space/SAI 1.15x/1.20x GPS IIIF $900 million, GEO $650 million photonics edge 95% launches. Commercial/CAM 0.98x/1.05x but inflecting with 777X $1.4 billion eVTOL $450 million MRO 35% China C919. Supply normalized titanium dual Japan/India 18 months inventory, rare earths DLA 85%, GTF 95% adherence vs. Red Sea/UC Rusal.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
Regarding program margins and cost performance, any updates on F-35 or NGAD EACs?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
David, margins strong at 11.8% overall. F-35 Lots 15/16 13.2% CPI 1.08 $285 million variance automation 18% learning absorbing titanium; KC-46 10.9% SPI 0.97 $150 million EAC digital. NGAD FPD 8.5% invoking $420 million changes CAS compliant. Missiles LRASM 16.8% CPI 1.12 22% additive, PrSM 15.2%; Space Orion 10.1% GPS 11.5% GaN 92%. Productivity 450 bps AI/Lean offsets inflation, sustainment mix.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation across all domains.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
